name: Character Key Shortcuts
explanation: If a site defines a keyboard shortcut using only letters, numbers, punctuation, or symbols, with no modifier key like Ctrl or Alt, then at least one of three things must be true: the user can turn the shortcut off, the user can remap it to include a modifier key, or the shortcut only takes effect while a specific control has focus. A single-letter shortcut like pressing "s" to open search is convenient for some, but without one of these safeguards it silently fires whenever a speech-input user simply speaks a word containing that letter, or whenever a user with a hand tremor brushes the key by accident.
whoItAffects: Speech-input users dictate text by speaking, and their software converts spoken letters into keystrokes; a single-letter shortcut can trigger unexpectedly while they're just trying to type a word containing that letter, disrupting or derailing what they're doing. People with fine-motor impairments or hand tremors can trigger a shortcut by accidentally brushing a key. Keyboard users who don't expect single-key shortcuts may trigger unintended actions while trying to type in a nearby field that isn't properly focused.
howToTest: Check the site's documentation or help menu for any single-key shortcuts made of letters, numbers, or punctuation with no modifier key like Ctrl, Alt, or Cmd. For each one, confirm at least one of: a settings page lets you turn it off, a settings page lets you remap it to include a modifier key, or it only activates while a specific element has keyboard focus rather than firing globally across the whole page. If none of those is true, try typing that letter into an unrelated text field elsewhere on the page — if the shortcut fires anyway, that's the failure this criterion is meant to catch.

check.question: A web app lets users press "/" anywhere on the page to jump straight to the search box, with no setting to disable or remap it, and the shortcut fires even while typing inside other text fields. Does this pass SC 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts?
choices: Yes, because "/" is a punctuation character, not a letter
No, because the shortcut has no off switch, no remapping option, and isn't limited to a focused control
Yes, because keyboard shortcuts always improve accessibility
It depends on whether the search box is visible on screen
